Chiral topological semimetals are phases of matter that host robust band crossings and topologically protected surface states. So far, their interesting properties have been believed to be restricted to the realm of perfect crystals. In this work, the authors show how they can survive strong structural disorder, challenging the view that disorder inevitably destroys this topological state. Using analytical theory, symmetry-group methods, numerical calculations, and a novel amorphous Wilson-loop technique, they demonstrate that Weyl and higher-charge chiral fermions can persist even in amorphous metals. Long-range order in local structural chirality stabilizes these phases. This understanding suggests pathways for engineering such geometry-enforced topological behavior in strongly disordered systems, opening up new possibilities for investigating these phases of matter and exploring their potential applications.

We present new precise data on the helicity-dependent total inclusive photoabsorption cross section for the proton and the deuteron, verifying the validity of the GDH sum rule. While vortex stretching in turbulence is commonly understood in analogy to material line stretching, the viscous tilting of vorticity prevents sustained alignment with material lines. In this paper, it is shown via numerical simulation that the surgical removal of viscous tilting from the vorticity evolution equations in isotropic turbulence results in dramatic deviations from basic turbulence scaling laws. These observations demonstrate that the viscous tilting of vorticity, and thus the difference between vorticity stretching and that of material lines, is an essential characteristic of turbulence.

Adiabatic Thouless pumps, which undergird the modern theory of polarization, have potential applications ranging from metrology to adiabatic quantum computing. Here, the authors use counterdiabatic driving to develop a non-adiabatic Thouless pump. Their analytic model, which has only nearest neighbor interactions, exhibits exactly quantized charge pumping that is topologically robust to disorder, and dynamically robust to disorder and noise for sufficiently rapid driving – which the authors demonstrate is a universal feature of counterdiabatic driving. The fast, robust and locally tuned pump cycle also models qubit flips, which may have quantum hardware applications.

This work temporarily reshapes the governing physics into a smooth problem that can be solved exactly. The reshaped problem delivers not only a blueprint for the device but also a map of its own uncertainty, showing where to trust the blueprint and where to keep exploring. Across eight distinct photonic and microwave design tasks, this convex preoptimization consistently beats conventional stop-and-restart sweeps while using a fraction of the computing time.
